# `Q-5-31` — Nested Projects Skipped

> One or more subdirectories contain their own `_quarto.yml` (or
> `_quarto.yaml`). Their files belong to those nested projects, so
> this project's render list skipped them.

## What this means

A directory with its own `_quarto.yml` is a project of its own, even
when it sits inside another project. Quarto 2 treats it as a
boundary: the files under it belong to the nested project, and they
render with the nested project's config when you run
`q2 render <dir>`.

The outer project's implicit patterns stop at that boundary.
Implicit patterns are the default `**/*.qmd`, and any glob that
doesn't name the nested directory (for example `**/*.md` or
`*/page.qmd`). The warning lists every nested project whose files one
of these patterns would otherwise have matched. For example:

```
my-site/
├── _quarto.yml        ← outer project
├── index.qmd          ← rendered
└── sub/
    ├── _quarto.yml    ← nested project
    └── page.qmd       ← skipped by the outer render (Q-5-31)
```

The warning appears once per render and names every skipped
directory.

## Quarto 1 differs

Quarto 1 ignores a nested `_quarto.yml` when rendering the outer
project, without any warning. It renders `sub/page.qmd` as part of
the outer site, with the outer chrome and outer metadata. But
`quarto render sub` renders the same page with the nested config. The
file's owner therefore depends on which command you run. Quarto 2
makes the nearest `_quarto.yml` the owner in both cases.

If you are migrating a Quarto 1 project and pages under a
subdirectory disappeared from the site, this is why.

## How to fix it

Pick whichever matches what the directory is:

- **It really is a separate project.** Render it on its own with
  `q2 render sub`. To keep this warning quiet, exclude the directory
  in the outer project's render list:

  ```yaml
  project:
    render:
      - "!sub/**"
  ```

  A list of only `!` patterns still renders the default `**/*.qmd`,
  so this subtracts just the nested project.

- **It only holds settings for that directory.** Rename its
  `_quarto.yml` to `_metadata.yml`. A `_metadata.yml` merges its
  settings into every document in the directory, and the directory
  stays part of the outer project.

- **You want specific pages from it rendered in the outer site.**
  List them by a path that names the directory, such as
  `sub/page.qmd`, `sub/*.qmd` or `sub`. They render with the outer
  project's config, and you get [`Q-5-32`](Q-5-32.qmd) as a reminder.

The `!` exclusion is the way to silence this warning.
`diagnostics: {Q-5-31: off}` does not work for it yet, because the
`diagnostics:` key only applies to per-document warnings and this one
is reported once for the whole project.
